text:
Priya: quick check-in on the idle compactor prototype I pushed. added a background worker that opportunistically coalesces free runs in arenas when device(s) are quiet. link: https://gh/rdw/idle-compact-proto.
Ben: saw it. what triggers a run? any chance this blocks allocation hot-paths?
Priya: run starts when device idle >150ms and fragmentation ratio >25% for an arena. worker uses per-arena try_lock and falls back immediately if contested. we avoid global mutexes.
Hoa: 150ms seems short; infra noise could flip it. can we make it adaptive?
Priya: good point. plan is adaptive idle: baseline 150ms but multiply by 2x if p99 small-batch latency rises, tracked per-cluster.
Diego: how are we coordinating with evictor and paging? We can't move pages that are pinned or in peer mappings.
Priya: compactor queries evictor for a compact token for an arena-range. evictor will refuse if pages have active pins or if peer-mapped across devices. token includes allowed_bytes and a pcie_bps budget.
Ben: token model sounds sane. avoids races where both evictor and compactor try to rehome a page. is the token sync local?
Priya: yes, token handshake is host-local over the existing admission channel. no RPCs across machines. cheap and lock-free on the common path.
Hoa: we should record compact.requested and compact.denied metrics with reasons (pinned, in-flight, cross-device). that'll help triage denies.
Priya: added as todo in PR. also planning compact.bytes_moved, compact.duration_ms, compact.yields.
Diego: PCIe thrash is a worry. are we rate-limiting DMA?
Priya: compactor schedules device-to-device memcpy with a token bucket. default cap is 300MB/s per-device but tunable via runtime.conf. if we hit cap we yield and reschedule later.
Ben: what's the correctness model for CUDA streams? compaction shouldn't reorder tensors needed by an active stream.
Priya: we only compact objects with refcount==0 and no active CUDA events. we query the stream registry; if any recent interaction exists we skip.
Hoa: rollout strategy? I'd prefer feature-flagged growth with canary telemetry and an automatic off ramp.
Priya: plan: default disabled. enable on rdw-canary-5 and rdw-canary-6 for 48h, collect frag_reduction, OOM_rate, p50/p95/p99. auto-disable if p99 increases >7% for >20m.
Diego: integration tests? need a harness that simulates small-batch inference with pinned bookkeeping and peer mappings. also a synthetic workload that holds many small allocations to stress fragmentation.
Priya: adding tests: (1) pinned-heavy: ensure compactor skips; (2) peer-spread: ensure token denied; (3) microbatch-latency: ensure no regressions under controlled load.
Ben: minor API Q: should allocator push candidate ranges to evictor or should evictor be asked? who owns the view of fragmentation?
Priya: allocator proposes ranges and asks for tokens. evictor retains final say. keeps single source of truth for admission.
Hoa: locking again: compactor mustn't spin waiting on arena locks. prefer try_lock with exponential backoff into scheduler yield.
Priya: implemented try_lock + backoff + max_attempts = 3 then give up for that run.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: runtime image rdw/rvv:idle-compact-v1 deployed to rdw-canary-5 at 6832100065.
Diego: let's also add a lightweight histogram compact.reclaim_ms_per_kb to see efficiency.
Priya: adding that. also setting logs to sample 1% to avoid noise.
Ben: one last ask: expose a per-tenant opt-out flag (console) so customers worried about PCIe impact can disable per-tenant.
Priya: will add tenant-level toggle and an enterprise policy in console.
Hoa: great. once tests land I'll run the canary suite and report back.
Priya: thanks all, pushing an update with metrics and config in a bit.
